summary: The paper establishes optimal closed-form potential parameters, minimal-degree Newton-Binomial filtering, and tightened M-matrix bounds for deterministic subexponential discrete logarithms. Rigorously backed by 20 constructive Lean 4 theorems and 16 zero-float certificates, it achieves 64x-227x threshold compression and exact finite-dimensional tightness.
strengths: Exact closed-form derivation of optimal penalty lambda* via non-calculus Cauchy-Schwarz square identities.
Rigorous proof and construction of the minimal-degree (4w-2) nonnegative Newton-Binomial filter, saving 4 series terms and precision bits.
Tightened Fischer-Hadamard M-matrix determinant bounds and complete formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 with zero axioms and zero sorry.
Comprehensive zero-float Python verification suite with 56 adversarial tests and 16 SHA-256 certificates.
weaknesses: Reliance on the Cauchy-Hermite Boolean tensor contraction primitive remains conditional.
High mathematical density requires careful study of the algebraic identities.
